I5.quote: In this study, we compressed hydrogen up to 70 MPa in a non-mechanical device based on cyclic, thermally driven, hydrogen adsorption/desorption on activated carbon (AC).

notes: Experimental paper on a 0.5 L thermally driven H2 compressor (MSC-30 and MSP20X activated carbons, charged at 77 K, 4-8 MPa) but it reports no H2 uptake of its own. Results are tank pressure vs temperature/time (Figs 3, 4, 8, 10), a discharge flow of 28 NL/h at 70 MPa (Fig 9c, flowmeter FT 2) and a compressed-H2-mass-to-tank-volume ratio of 0.951 g/L (Section 4.5). These describe H2 released on heating and are normalised to tank volume, not sorbent mass; none is an amount taken up from the gas phase. Charging flowmeter FT 1 is used only to detect end of charging (Section 2.3). Adsorbed amounts (Fig 7a, Eq. 20, MDA model) are computed, with parameters from earlier study [7]. The 4.8 wt% uptake for MSP20X (Section 4.4) and BET areas 3305 and 2363 m2/g (Table 1) are quoted from [7]. Borderline point for a third reader: whether the FT 2 discharge flow counts as a flow-method uptake measurement; read here as desorption output, so I1 is not met. Paper is experimental, so not theoretical_only; not electrochemical, not a review, not retracted (record is_retracted false, no retraction notice in text). duplicate_data not applied: the paper does not state that all its uptake values were published before, it reports none of its own. Code follows the I1-failure rule (no H2 uptake value, so none with stated T and P).
